question: Your organization runs many workloads in different Google Cloud projects, each linked to the same billing account. Each project's workload costs can vary from month to month, but the overall combined cost of all projects is relatively stable. Your organization needs to optimize its cost. What should your organization do?

options.A: Purchase a commitment per project for each project's usual minimum
options.B: Create a billing account per project, and link each project to a different billing account
options.C: Turn on committed use discount sharing, and create a commitment for the combined usage
options.D: Move all workloads from all different projects into one single consolidated project

explanations.A: Incorrect. Buying a separate commitment per project for each project's minimum wastes the discount, because usage that spikes in one project cannot offset another project's dip; it does not capture the stable combined total.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Splitting projects across multiple billing accounts prevents commitments and discounts from being shared, so it increases administrative overhead without optimizing cost.
explanations.C: Correct. Committed use discount (CUD) sharing pools usage across all projects under the same billing account, so a single commitment sized to the stable combined total is fully consumed even when individual projects fluctuate, maximizing the discount.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Consolidating all workloads into one project would destroy the resource segregation, isolation, and access boundaries that separate projects provide, and is unnecessary because CUD sharing already aggregates usage for billing.

question: How should a multinational organization that is migrating to Google Cloud consider security and privacy regulations to ensure that it is in compliance with global standards?

options.A: Comply with data security and privacy regulations in each geographical region
options.B: Comply with regional standards for data security and privacy, because they supersede all international regulations
options.C: Comply with international standards for data security and privacy, because they supersede all regional regulations
options.D: Comply with regional data security regulations, because they're more complex than privacy standards

explanations.A: Correct. A multinational organization must meet the data security and privacy laws of every region in which it operates (such as GDPR in Europe), because data residency and compliance obligations are jurisdiction-specific and apply wherever data is collected, processed, or stored.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Regional standards do not automatically supersede international ones; the organization must satisfy all applicable regulations in each jurisdiction, not assume one set overrides others.
explanations.C: Incorrect. International standards do not override regional laws; local regulations such as data residency rules still apply and must be honored independently.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Complexity is not the basis for prioritizing one regulation over another, and ignoring privacy standards in favor of security regulations would leave the organization non-compliant.

question: Your organization wants to optimize its use of Google Cloud's discounts on virtual machine-based workloads. You plan to use 200 CPUs constantly for the next 3 years, and you forecast that spikes of up to 300 CPUs will occur approximately 30% of the time. What should you choose?

options.A: 1-year committed use discount for 200 CPUs
options.B: 3-year committed use discount for 300 CPUs
options.C: 3-year committed use discount for 200 CPUs

explanations.A: Incorrect. A 1-year commitment gives a smaller discount than a 3-year commitment, and you have committed steady demand for 3 full years, so it does not maximize savings.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Committing to 300 CPUs would mean paying for 300 CPUs all the time even though the extra 100 are only needed 30% of the time, wasting the commitment for 70% of the period.
explanations.C: Correct. A 3-year CUD for the constant baseline of 200 CPUs gives the deepest discount on guaranteed usage, while the occasional spikes to 300 are best handled separately by on-demand capacity, optimizing total cost.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pay-as-you-go applies no commitment discount to the steady 200-CPU baseline you will run for 3 years, so it is the most expensive option for that predictable usage.

question: Your organization needs to minimize how much it pays for data traffic from the Google network to the internet. What should your organization do?

options.A: Choose the Standard network service tier.
options.B: Choose the Premium network service tier.
options.C: Deploy Cloud VPN.

explanations.A: Correct. The Standard network service tier routes egress traffic over the public internet for as much of the path as possible, which costs less than the Premium tier, minimizing the price paid for internet-bound traffic.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The Premium tier delivers traffic over Google's high-performance global backbone and is more expensive, so it does not minimize egress cost.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud VPN creates an encrypted tunnel for connecting networks (for example to on-premises), not a mechanism for lowering general internet egress pricing.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud NAT lets instances without external IP addresses reach the internet; it provides address translation, not reduced egress data-transfer pricing.

question: Your organization wants to migrate your on-premises environment to Google Cloud. The on-premises environment consists of containers and virtual machine instances. Which Google Cloud products can help to migrate the container images and the virtual machine disks?

options.A: Compute Engine and Filestore
options.B: Artifact Registry and Cloud Storage
options.C: Dataflow and BigQuery

explanations.A: Incorrect. Compute Engine runs VMs and Filestore provides managed NFS file storage; neither is the repository for storing container images, so they do not address migrating container artifacts.
explanations.B: Correct. Artifact Registry stores and manages container images, while Cloud Storage can hold the virtual machine disk images, so together they cover migrating both containers and VM disks.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Dataflow processes data pipelines and BigQuery is a data warehouse; these are analytics services, not tools for storing container images or VM disks.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Pub/Sub is a messaging service for event streams; although Cloud Storage could hold disk images, Pub/Sub does not store container images, so the pair is not appropriate.

question: Your company security team manages access control to production systems using an LDAP directory group. How is this access control managed in the Google Cloud production project?

options.A: Assign the proper role to the Service Account in the project's IAM Policy
options.B: Grant each user the roles/iam.serviceAccountUser role on a service account that exists in the Google Group.
options.C: Assign the proper role to the Google Group in the project's IAM Policy.
options.D: Create the project in a folder with the same name as the LDAP directory group.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A service account represents an application or workload identity, not the human LDAP group members, so granting it the role would not give those users access.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The serviceAccountUser role lets a principal impersonate a service account; it does not map LDAP group membership to project permissions and a service account does not live inside a Google Group.
explanations.C: Correct. The LDAP group is synced to a Google Group (for example via Google Cloud Directory Sync), and assigning the appropriate IAM role to that group means access automatically follows group membership, which is Google's recommended practice.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Naming a folder after the group has no effect on access; IAM permissions are granted through policy bindings, not by matching folder names to group names.

question: Your organization wants to be sure that is expenditures on cloud services are in line with the budget. Which two Google Cloud cost management features help your organization gain greater visibility into its cloud resource costs? (Choose two.)

options.A: Billing dashboards
options.B: Resource labels
options.C: Sustained use discounts

explanations.A: Correct. Billing dashboards (such as the Cloud Billing reports and Looker Studio integrations) visualize spend over time and by service, giving direct visibility into cloud resource costs.
explanations.B: Correct. Resource labels are key-value tags that let you categorize resources by team, environment, or cost center, so billing data can be broken down and attributed, improving cost visibility.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Sustained use discounts automatically reduce cost for long-running resources; they lower the bill but are a discount mechanism, not a visibility feature.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Financial governance policies (like budgets, alerts, and quotas) help control and enforce spending, but the question specifically asks about features for gaining visibility.
explanations.E: Incorrect. A payments profile stores billing identity and payment instrument details; it is for processing payments, not for analyzing or surfacing resource cost visibility.

question: Your organization needs to process large amounts of data from an online application that operates continuously. You do not want to be required to provision infrastructure or create server clusters. What should your organization choose?

options.A: Compute Engine with BigQuery
options.B: Dataproc
options.C: Google Kubernetes Engine with Cloud Bigtable

explanations.A: Incorrect. Compute Engine requires you to provision and manage VM instances, so it does not meet the requirement of avoiding infrastructure provisioning.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Dataproc is managed Hadoop/Spark but still requires you to create and size clusters, which conflicts with not wanting to manage server clusters.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Google Kubernetes Engine requires you to manage node pools and clusters, so it is not a serverless, no-provisioning option.
explanations.D: Correct. Dataflow is a fully managed, serverless service for stream and batch data processing that autoscales without you provisioning infrastructure or managing clusters, fitting a continuously operating application.

question: Your organization needs to ensure that the Google Cloud resources of each of your departments are segregated from one another. Each department has several environments of its own: development, testing, and production. Which strategy should your organization choose?

options.A: Create a project per department, and create a folder per environment in each project.
options.B: Create a folder per department, and create a project per environment in each folder.
options.C: Create a Cloud Identity domain per department, and create a project per environment in each domain.
options.D: Create a Cloud Identity domain per environment, and create a project per department in each domain.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Folders cannot be nested inside projects; projects are the lowest level of the hierarchy, so you cannot create a folder per environment within a project.
explanations.B: Correct. A folder per department provides departmental segregation and shared policy inheritance, and a project per environment inside each folder isolates development, testing, and production resources, matching Google's recommended resource hierarchy.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Identity is for managing users and groups, not for segregating cloud resources; an organization typically has a single Cloud Identity domain, not one per department.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Creating a Cloud Identity domain per environment misuses Cloud Identity, which manages identities rather than environment isolation, and does not provide proper departmental resource segregation.

question: Your organization is defining the resource hierarchy for its new application in Google Cloud. You need separate development and production environments. The production environment will be deployed in Compute Engine in two regions. Which structure should your organization choose?

options.A: Create a single project for all environments. Use labels to segregate resources by environment.
options.B: Create a single project for all environments. Use tags to segregate resources by environment.
options.C: Create one project for the development environment and one project for the production environment.
options.D: Create two projects for the development environment and two projects for the production environment (one for each

explanations.A: Incorrect. Putting all environments in one project and using labels does not provide true isolation; a mistake in development could affect production because they share the same project boundary and IAM policy.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Like labels, tags do not create a security or isolation boundary between environments; a single shared project leaves development and production exposed to each other.
explanations.C: Correct. Using a separate project for development and a separate project for production gives each environment its own isolation, IAM policies, and quotas; a single production project can span two regions, so no extra projects are required.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A project is a global container that can host resources in multiple regions, so creating one project per region is unnecessary and adds management overhead without added isolation benefit.

question: Your organization meant to purchase a 3-year Committed Use Discount, but accidentally purchased a 1-year Committed Use Discount instead. What should your organization do?

options.A: Contact your financial institution.
options.B: Contact Trust and Safety.
options.C: Contact Cloud Billing Support.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A financial institution handles your bank or card, not Google Cloud commitments; it cannot change a committed use discount term.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Trust and Safety handles abuse, policy violations, and account security issues, not billing or commitment purchase corrections.
explanations.C: Correct. Cloud Billing Support is the team responsible for billing matters including committed use discounts, so they can help review or correct a mistakenly purchased commitment.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Technical Support assists with product configuration and technical issues, whereas a wrong commitment purchase is a billing matter handled by Cloud Billing Support.

question: Your organization needs to allow a production job to have access to a BigQuery dataset. The production job is running on a Compute Engine instance that is part of an instance group. What should be included in the IAM Policy on the BigQuery dataset?

options.A: The Compute Engine instance group
options.B: The project that owns the Compute Engine instance
options.C: The Compute Engine service account

explanations.A: Incorrect. An instance group is not an IAM identity; you cannot grant permissions to it, and instances in the group authenticate using their service account.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Granting access to the whole project would give every resource in the project access to the dataset, violating least privilege rather than scoping access to the specific job.
explanations.C: Correct. Workloads on Compute Engine authenticate as their attached service account, so granting the appropriate BigQuery role to that service account in the dataset's IAM policy gives the production job the access it needs.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An individual VM instance is not an IAM principal; access is granted to the service account it runs as, not to the instance itself.

question: Your team is publishing research results and needs to make large amounts of data available to other researchers within the professional community and the public at minimum cost. How should you host the data?

options.A: Use a Cloud Storage bucket and enable “Requester Pays.”
options.B: Use a Cloud Storage bucket and provide Signed URLs for the data files.
options.C: Use a Cloud Storage bucket and set up a Cloud Interconnect connection to allow access to the data.
options.D: Host the data on-premises, and set up a Cloud Interconnect connection to allow access to the data.

explanations.A: Correct. Requester Pays shifts data access and egress charges to the requester who downloads the data, so the publishing team can share large datasets broadly while minimizing its own cost.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Signed URLs grant time-limited access to specific files and the bucket owner still pays egress; they are designed for controlled sharing, not minimizing cost for wide public distribution.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Interconnect provides dedicated private connectivity for an organization's own network and incurs significant cost; it is not how you make public research data broadly available.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Hosting on-premises with Cloud Interconnect adds infrastructure and connectivity costs and does not provide cheap, scalable public access compared with Cloud Storage.

question: Your company needs to segment Google Cloud resources used by each team from the others. The teams' efforts are changing frequently, and you need to reduce operational risk and maintain cost visibility. Which approach does Google recommend?

options.A: One project per team.
options.B: One organization per team.
options.C: One project that contains all of each team's resources.

explanations.A: Incorrect. A single project per team is too coarse for teams that frequently change and run multiple workloads or environments, limiting flexibility and isolation.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An organization node represents the whole company and is tied to one domain; you cannot reasonably create a separate organization per team.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Putting all of a team's resources in one project provides no internal isolation and makes frequent change riskier, the opposite of reducing operational risk.
explanations.D: Correct. A top-level folder per team lets each team contain its own projects, applies IAM policies and budgets at the folder level for cost visibility, and isolates teams to reduce operational risk, which is Google's recommended hierarchy for this scenario.

question: How do Migrate for Compute Engine and Migrate for Anthos differ?

options.A: Unlike Migrate for Anthos, Migrate for Compute Engine assumes that the migration source is VMware vSphere.
options.B: Migrate for Compute Engine charges for ingress, but Migrate for Anthos does not.
options.C: Migrate for Compute Engine is closed source, and Migrate for Anthos is open source.
options.D: Migrate for Anthos migrates to containers, and Migrate for Compute Engine migrates to virtual machines.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Both tools can migrate from various sources; Migrate for Compute Engine is not limited to assuming a VMware vSphere source, so this is not the defining difference.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Google Cloud does not charge for ingress data transfer, and pricing is not the distinguishing factor between these two migration tools.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The open- versus closed-source distinction is not what separates these products; the meaningful difference is the migration target.
explanations.D: Correct. Migrate for Anthos modernizes workloads by moving them into containers running on GKE/Anthos, whereas Migrate for Compute Engine moves workloads as virtual machines onto Compute Engine, which is the key difference between the two.

question: Your large and frequently changing organization's user information is stored in an on-premises LDAP database. The database includes user passwords and group and organization membership. How should your organization provision Google accounts and groups to access Google Cloud resources?

options.A: Replicate the LDAP infrastructure on Compute Engine
options.B: Use the Firebase Authentication REST API to create users
options.C: Use Google Cloud Directory Sync to create users
options.D: Use the Identity Platform REST API to create users

explanations.A: Incorrect. Replicating LDAP on Compute Engine just moves the directory into the cloud without integrating it with Cloud Identity, so it does not provision Google accounts and groups.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Firebase Authentication manages end-user sign-in for apps, not corporate workforce identities for accessing Google Cloud resources.
explanations.C: Correct. Google Cloud Directory Sync (GCDS) automatically synchronizes users and groups from an on-premises LDAP directory such as Active Directory into Cloud Identity, keeping Google accounts and group membership up to date for a large, frequently changing organization.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Identity Platform provides authentication for customer-facing applications, not synchronization of an internal LDAP directory into Google Cloud admin identities.

question: Your organization recently migrated its compute workloads to Google Cloud. You want these workloads in Google Cloud to privately and securely access your large volume of on-premises data, and you also want to minimize latency. What should your organization do?

options.A: Use Storage Transfer Service to securely make your data available to Google Cloud
options.B: Create a VPC between your on-premises data center and your Google resources
options.C: Peer your on-premises data center to Google's Edge Network
options.D: Use Transfer Appliance to securely make your data available to Google Cloud

explanations.A: Incorrect. Storage Transfer Service copies data into Cloud Storage; it is a one-time or scheduled migration tool, not a way to give workloads ongoing private, low-latency access to data that stays on-premises.
explanations.B: Correct. Establishing private connectivity between the on-premises data center and Google Cloud through a VPC (using Cloud VPN or Cloud Interconnect) provides secure, private, low-latency access to the on-premises data without traversing the public internet.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Edge Network peering optimizes delivery of Google's services and content to users; it does not provide private connectivity for workloads to reach an organization's on-premises data.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Transfer Appliance is a physical device for shipping large data volumes into Google Cloud, a one-way migration method, not a means of ongoing private access to data kept on-premises.

question: Your organization consists of many teams. Each team has many Google Cloud projects. Your organization wants to simplify the management of identity and access policies for these projects. How can you group these projects to meet this goal?

options.A: Group each team's projects into a separate domain
options.B: Assign labels based on the virtual machines that are part of each team's projects
options.C: Use folders to group each team's projects
options.D: Group each team's projects into a separate organization node

explanations.A: Incorrect. A domain corresponds to a Cloud Identity organization and is not a grouping mechanism within the resource hierarchy for organizing teams' projects.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Labels are metadata for billing and organization; they do not group projects for the purpose of applying IAM policies through inheritance.
explanations.C: Correct. Folders group related projects and allow IAM policies set at the folder level to be inherited by all contained projects, simplifying identity and access management across each team's projects.
explanations.D: Incorrect. An organization node is the single root of the entire company's hierarchy; you cannot create a separate organization node per team for grouping projects.

question: An organization needs to categorize text-based customer reviews on their website using a pre-trained machine learning model. Which Google Cloud product or service should the organization use?

options.A: Cloud Natural Language API
options.B: Dialogflow
options.C: Recommendations AI

explanations.A: Correct. The Cloud Natural Language API is a pre-trained service that analyzes text for sentiment, entities, and classification, letting the organization categorize customer reviews without building or training a model.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Dialogflow builds conversational interfaces such as chatbots and virtual agents; it is not designed for classifying existing text reviews.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Recommendations AI generates product recommendations for users, not categorization of text reviews.
explanations.D: Incorrect. TensorFlow is a framework for building and training custom models from scratch, which contradicts the requirement to use a pre-trained model.

question: An organization is planning its cloud expenditure. What should the organization do to control costs?

options.A: Consider cloud resource costs as capital expenditure in annual planning.
options.B: Use only cloud resources; they have no cloud infrastructure costs.
options.C: Review cloud resource costs frequently because costs depend on usage.
options.D: Assess cloud resources costs only when SLO is not met by their cloud provider.

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud spending is an operating expense (OpEx) that varies with usage, not a fixed capital expenditure planned once a year, so treating it as CapEx does not control ongoing costs.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud resources do incur costs based on consumption; claiming they have no infrastructure cost is simply false.
explanations.C: Correct. Because cloud follows a pay-as-you-go model where cost scales with usage, reviewing costs frequently lets the organization spot trends, catch anomalies, and adjust resources to stay within budget.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cost management is continuous and unrelated to whether an SLO is met; waiting for a service-level breach would leave spending uncontrolled in the meantime.

question: An organization is searching for an open-source machine learning platform to build and deploy their own custom machine learning applications using TPUs. Which Google Cloud product or service should the organization use?

options.A: TensorFlow
options.B: BigQuery ML
options.C: Vision API

explanations.A: Correct. TensorFlow is Google's open-source machine learning framework for building and deploying custom models, and it is optimized to run on TPUs, matching all of the stated requirements.
explanations.B: Incorrect. BigQuery ML lets you build models using SQL inside BigQuery; it is a managed feature, not an open-source platform for custom TPU-based applications.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The Vision API is a pre-trained image analysis service, not an open-source platform for building custom models.
explanations.D: Incorrect. AutoML Vision trains custom image models with minimal coding but is a managed, proprietary service, not an open-source framework.

question: What is an example of unstructured data that organizations can capture from social media?

options.A: Post comments
options.B: Tagging
options.C: Profile picture

explanations.A: Correct. Post comments are free-form text that does not fit a fixed schema, which is the defining characteristic of unstructured data.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Tagging produces discrete, structured associations (for example linking a user or category) that can be stored in defined fields, so it is structured rather than unstructured.
explanations.C: Incorrect. While an image file is technically unstructured, a profile picture is a single defined attribute; the clearest example of free-form social media text is post comments.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Location is captured as structured values such as coordinates or place names that fit neatly into database fields, so it is structured data.

question: An organization relies on online seasonal sales for the majority of their annual revenue. Why should the organization use App Engine for their customer app?

options.A: Automatically adjusts physical inventory in real time
options.B: Autoscales during peaks in demand
options.C: Runs maintenance during seasonal sales
options.D: Recommends the right products to customers

explanations.A: Incorrect. App Engine is a platform for running applications; it does not manage or adjust physical inventory.
explanations.B: Correct. App Engine is a serverless platform that automatically scales instances up during demand spikes and back down afterward, which is ideal for the unpredictable traffic of seasonal sales.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Running maintenance during peak sales would be undesirable, and App Engine's value is handling load, not scheduling maintenance during sales.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Product recommendations come from machine learning services like Recommendations AI, not from the App Engine hosting platform itself.

question: An organization is using machine learning to make predictions. One of their datasets mistakenly includes mislabeled data. How will the prediction be impacted?

options.A: Increased risk of privacy leaks
options.B: Increased risk of inaccuracy
options.C: Decreased model compatibility

explanations.A: Incorrect. Mislabeled data affects correctness of learning, not the exposure of sensitive information, so it does not directly increase privacy leak risk.
explanations.B: Correct. Machine learning models learn from their training labels, so mislabeled data teaches the model incorrect patterns and increases the risk of inaccurate predictions.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Compatibility refers to how a model integrates with systems; mislabeled training data does not change compatibility, it degrades accuracy.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Training time depends on data volume and model complexity, not on whether labels are correct, so mislabeling does not reduce training time.

question: A global organization is developing an application to manage payments and online bank accounts in multiple regions. Each transaction must be handled consistently in their database, and they anticipate almost unlimited growth in the amount of data stored. Which Google Cloud product should the organization choose?

options.A: Cloud SQL
options.B: Cloud Spanner
options.C: Cloud Storage

explanations.A: Incorrect. Cloud SQL is a regional managed relational database with limited vertical scalability; it does not provide the global horizontal scale and strong consistency needed for nearly unlimited growth across regions.
explanations.B: Correct. Cloud Spanner is a globally distributed relational database that combines strong transactional consistency with horizontal scalability to virtually unlimited size, making it ideal for global financial transactions.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Storage is object storage for files and blobs, not a transactional relational database, so it cannot enforce consistent financial transactions.
explanations.D: Incorrect. BigQuery is an analytics data warehouse optimized for queries over large datasets, not for handling consistent real-time transactional writes for banking operations.

question: An organization has servers running mission-critical workloads on-premises around the world. They want to modernize their infrastructure with a multi-cloud architecture. What benefit could the organization experience?

options.A: Ability to disable regional network connectivity during cyber attacks
options.B: Ability to keep backups of their data on-premises in case of failure
options.C: Full management access to their regional infrastructure
options.D: Reduced likelihood of system failure during high demand events

explanations.A: Incorrect. Disabling regional connectivity is not a benefit of multi-cloud; the value of multi-cloud is spreading workloads, not cutting off networks during attacks.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Keeping backups on-premises is a hybrid/on-premises capability and does not describe the resilience benefit gained from a multi-cloud architecture.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Full management access to underlying infrastructure is characteristic of on-premises ownership; in cloud the provider manages much of the infrastructure.
explanations.D: Correct. Distributing workloads across multiple clouds adds redundancy and elastic capacity, so the organization is less likely to suffer system failure or outages during high-demand events.

question: An organization needs to run frequent updates for their business app. Why should the organization use Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE)?

options.A: Customer expectations can be adjusted without using marketing tools
options.B: Seamless changes can be made without causing any application downtime.
options.C: GKE handles version control seamlessly and out of the box
options.D: GKE is well suited for all monolithic applications

explanations.A: Incorrect. GKE is a container orchestration platform; it has nothing to do with adjusting customer expectations or marketing.
explanations.B: Correct. GKE supports rolling updates and other deployment strategies that gradually replace pods, allowing frequent application updates with zero or minimal downtime.
explanations.C: Incorrect. GKE orchestrates containers but does not provide source-code version control; that is the role of tools like Git or Cloud Source Repositories.
explanations.D: Incorrect. GKE is designed for containerized, often microservice-based workloads; monolithic applications do not inherently benefit and are not its ideal fit.

question: An organization wants to use Apigee to manage all their application programming interfaces (APIs). What will Apigee enable the organization to do?

options.A: Increase application privacy
options.B: Measure and track API performance
options.C: Analyze application development speed

explanations.A: Incorrect. While Apigee adds security controls, increasing privacy is not its defining purpose; it is an API management platform focused on the API lifecycle.
explanations.B: Correct. Apigee provides API analytics and monitoring so organizations can measure and track API performance, usage, latency, and error rates as a core capability.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Apigee manages APIs in production; it does not analyze the speed of the development process itself.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Although Apigee supports developer portals, its primary value is managing and analyzing APIs, not acting as a marketplace to sell them.

question: An e-commerce organization is reviewing their cloud data storage. What type of raw data can they store in a relational database without any processing?

options.A: Product inventory
options.B: Product photographs
options.C: Instructional videos

explanations.A: Correct. Product inventory is structured data with clear fields such as SKU, name, quantity, and price, which fits directly into the rows and columns of a relational database.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Photographs are unstructured binary objects best stored in object storage like Cloud Storage, not natively as relational rows and columns.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Videos are large unstructured media files suited to object storage, not to a relational database without processing.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Chat history is free-form unstructured text that does not fit a fixed relational schema without processing.

question: A hotel wants to modernize their legacy systems so that customers can make reservations through a mobile app. What's the benefit of using an application programming interface (API) to do this?

options.A: They do not have to develop the end-user application
options.B: They can deprecate their legacy systems
options.C: They can transform their systems to be cloud-native
options.D: They do not have to rewrite the legacy system

explanations.A: Incorrect. An API exposes functionality but the organization still needs to build the mobile app that consumes it, so it does not remove the need for an end-user application.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Using an API to front the legacy system keeps that system in use rather than deprecating it.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Adding an API does not by itself convert legacy systems into cloud-native architecture; it provides an access layer to the existing system.
explanations.D: Correct. An API can wrap the existing legacy system and expose its functionality to the new mobile app, so the organization can modernize the customer experience without rewriting the underlying legacy system.

question: An organization wants to digitize and share large volumes of historical text and images. Why is a public cloud a better option than an on-premises solution?

options.A: In-house hardware management
options.B: Provides physical encryption key
options.C: Cost-effective at scale

explanations.A: Incorrect. In-house hardware management is a characteristic of on-premises, and it is a burden the cloud removes, not a benefit of the cloud.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Providing a physical encryption key is not a distinguishing advantage of public cloud; cloud providers manage encryption in software and hardware on your behalf.
explanations.C: Correct. Public cloud lets the organization pay only for the storage and compute it uses and scale elastically, making it cost-effective at scale for large, growing volumes of digitized data.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Public cloud shifts spending from capital expenditure to operating expenditure rather than optimizing CapEx; reducing upfront CapEx is the typical cloud benefit.

question: An organization wants to develop an application that can be personalized to user preferences throughout the year. Why should they build a cloud-native application instead of modernizing their existing on-premises application?

options.A: Developers can rely on the cloud provider for all source code
options.B: Developers can launch new features in an agile way
options.C: IT managers can migrate existing application architecture without needing updates
options.D: IT managers can accelerate capital expenditure planning

explanations.A: Incorrect. The cloud provider supplies infrastructure and managed services, not the organization's application source code; developers still write their own code.
explanations.B: Correct. Cloud-native applications use microservices, containers, and CI/CD, enabling developers to build, test, and launch new features rapidly and iteratively, which suits an app that must continually adapt to user preferences.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Building cloud-native means re-architecting for the cloud, not migrating existing architecture unchanged; that describes a lift-and-shift, not cloud-native development.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Cloud-native shifts costs toward operating expenditure; accelerating capital expenditure planning is not the reason to choose it over modernizing on-premises.

question: Which technology allows organizations to run multiple computer operating systems on a single piece of physical hardware?

options.A: Hypervisor
options.B: Containers
options.C: Serverless computing

explanations.A: Correct. A hypervisor virtualizes physical hardware into multiple virtual machines, each able to run its own complete, independent operating system on the same physical host.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Containers share the host operating system kernel and isolate applications rather than running multiple separate operating systems.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Serverless computing abstracts the infrastructure entirely so developers do not manage operating systems at all; it is not a way to run multiple OSes on one host.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Open source describes a software licensing and development model, not a technology for running multiple operating systems on one machine.

question: An organization is making a strategic change to customer support in response to feedback. They plan to extend their helpline availability hours. Why is the organization making this change?

options.A: Users expect professional expertise
options.B: Users require personalization
options.C: Users expect always-on services

explanations.A: Incorrect. Professional expertise concerns the quality of support, not its hours of availability, so it does not explain extending the helpline hours.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Personalization is about tailoring service to the individual, not about being available more of the time.
explanations.C: Correct. Extending helpline hours toward round-the-clock coverage directly responds to users' expectation of always-on, anytime services in the digital era.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Regional access concerns where the service is available, not the hours of operation that the organization is extending.

question: An organization is migrating their business applications from on-premises to the cloud. How could this impact their operations and personnel costs?

options.A: Reduced on-premises infrastructure management costs
options.B: Increased on-premises hardware maintenance costs
options.C: Reduced cloud software licensing costs

explanations.A: Correct. Moving to the cloud transfers responsibility for managing physical infrastructure to the provider, so the organization spends less staff time and money maintaining on-premises hardware and facilities.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Migrating away from on-premises reduces, rather than increases, hardware maintenance costs as workloads leave the data center.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Migration does not inherently reduce software licensing costs, and licensing is unrelated to the operations and personnel savings the move provides.
explanations.D: Incorrect. In the cloud the provider manages the underlying hardware, so the customer does not incur increased hardware management costs.

question: A retail company stores their product inventory in a legacy system. Often, customers find products on the company's website and want to purchase them in-store. However, when they arrive, they discover that the products are out of stock. How could the company benefit from using an application programming interface (API)?

options.A: To create personalized product recommendations for customers
options.B: To optimize their on-premises legacy system stability
options.C: By manually linking each inventory system to the website on a case-by-case basis
options.D: By programmatically connecting the inventory system to their website

explanations.A: Incorrect. Personalized recommendations are a separate feature and do not solve the problem of the website showing inaccurate stock availability.
explanations.B: Incorrect. An API exposes and integrates the legacy system's data; it is not a tool for tuning that system's internal stability.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The value of an API is automated, programmatic integration; manual case-by-case linking is exactly what an API replaces.
explanations.D: Correct. An API can programmatically connect the legacy inventory system to the website so stock levels are reflected in real time, preventing customers from traveling to the store for out-of-stock items.

question: An organization is training a machine learning model to predict extreme weather events in their country. How should they collect data to maximize prediction accuracy?

options.A: Collect all weather data evenly across all cities
options.B: Collect all weather data primarily from at-risk cities
options.C: Collect extreme weather data evenly across all cities
options.D: Collect extreme weather data primarily from at-risk cities

explanations.A: Correct. Collecting all weather data evenly across all cities gives the model a complete, representative, and unbiased dataset of both normal and extreme conditions everywhere, which maximizes its ability to accurately predict extreme events.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Focusing primarily on at-risk cities biases the dataset toward certain locations, so the model would generalize poorly to the rest of the country.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Collecting only extreme weather data omits the normal-condition baseline the model needs to distinguish extreme events from ordinary weather.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Limiting to extreme data from at-risk cities combines two biases, missing both normal conditions and geographic coverage, which harms accuracy.

question: An organization needs to search an application's source code to identify a potential issue. The application is distributed across multiple containers. Which Google Cloud product should the organization use?

options.A: Google Cloud Console
options.B: Cloud Trace
options.C: Cloud Monitoring

explanations.A: Incorrect. The Cloud Console is the general web UI for managing Google Cloud; it is not the dedicated tool for searching application logs to diagnose an issue.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Cloud Trace analyzes request latency and distributed traces for performance, not searching log output to find the source of an issue.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Cloud Monitoring collects metrics, dashboards, and alerts on system health, but does not provide searchable log entries of application events.
explanations.D: Correct. Cloud Logging aggregates and indexes logs from across all containers, letting the organization search log entries to identify and troubleshoot the issue in the distributed application.

question: An organization's web developers and operations personnel use different systems. How will increasing communication between the teams reduce issues caused by silos?

options.A: By assigning blame for failures and establishing consequences
options.B: By combining job role responsibilities to ensure that everyone has shared access
options.C: By increasing data encryption to strengthen workflows
options.D: By emphasizing shared ownership of business outcomes

explanations.A: Incorrect. Assigning blame creates a culture of fear that worsens silos; DevOps culture favors blameless approaches over punishment.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Simply merging job roles and granting everyone shared access is not the cultural fix; collaboration comes from shared goals, not from indiscriminate access.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Increasing data encryption is a security control and has nothing to do with breaking down communication silos between teams.
explanations.D: Correct. DevOps culture breaks down silos by having developers and operations share ownership of business outcomes, which aligns incentives, improves collaboration, and reduces friction between the teams.

question: How does a large hotel chain benefit from storing their customer reservation data in the cloud?

options.A: On-premises hardware access to transaction data
options.B: Real-time data transformation at scale within an on-premises database
options.C: Real-time business transaction accuracy at scale
options.D: Physical hardware access during peak demand

explanations.A: Incorrect. On-premises hardware access is the opposite of a cloud benefit; the cloud removes the need to manage physical hardware.
explanations.B: Incorrect. This describes processing within an on-premises database, not a benefit of storing the data in the cloud.
explanations.C: Correct. Cloud databases scale elastically and provide consistent, real-time transactional accuracy, so a hotel chain can handle reservations reliably across many locations even at high volume.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Physical hardware access is an on-premises characteristic; the cloud's elastic capacity, not hardware access, is what handles peak demand.

question: An organization wants to migrate legacy applications currently hosted in their data center to the cloud. The current architecture dictates that each application needs its own operating system (OS) instead of sharing an OS. Which infrastructure solution should they choose?

options.A: Virtual machines
options.B: Open source
options.C: Serverless computing

explanations.A: Correct. Virtual machines each include their own full, isolated operating system, which directly satisfies the requirement that each application run on its own OS rather than a shared one.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Open source is a software licensing model, not an infrastructure solution for providing each application a separate operating system.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Serverless computing abstracts away the operating system entirely, so it cannot satisfy a requirement for each application to have its own OS.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Containers share the host operating system kernel, which is exactly the shared-OS model the requirement rules out.

question: An organization operates their entire IT infrastructure from Google Cloud. What should they do to prepare for data breaches?

options.A: Reduce reliance on multi-factor authentication
options.B: Data security is Google's responsibility, so preparation is minimal
options.C: Create an incident plan to mitigate impacts
options.D: Strengthen their data center perimeter security

explanations.A: Incorrect. Reducing multi-factor authentication weakens security and increases breach risk, the opposite of preparing for breaches.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Under the shared responsibility model, the customer remains responsible for securing their data, identities, and access; security is not solely Google's responsibility.
explanations.C: Correct. Preparing an incident response plan lets the organization detect, contain, and recover from breaches quickly, mitigating their impact, which is its responsibility in the shared responsibility model.
explanations.D: Incorrect. With infrastructure running in Google Cloud rather than a private data center, hardening a physical data center perimeter is not the relevant breach preparation.

question: An organization wants to transform multiple types of structured and unstructured data in the cloud from various sources. The data must be readily accessible for analysis and insights. Which cloud data storage system should the organization use?

options.A: Relational database
options.B: Private data center
options.C: Data field

explanations.A: Incorrect. A relational database is optimized for structured transactional data, not for consolidating diverse structured and unstructured sources for large-scale analysis.
explanations.B: Incorrect. A private data center is a hosting location, not a cloud data storage system designed for analytics across varied data.
explanations.C: Incorrect. A data field is just a single attribute within a record, not a storage system for analyzing data from many sources.
explanations.D: Correct. A data warehouse (such as BigQuery) consolidates and transforms data from many sources and makes it readily queryable for analysis and insights, fitting the requirement.

question: An organization wants to use all available data to offer predictive suggestions on their website that improve over time. Which method should the organization use?

options.A: Data automation
options.B: Trends analysis
options.C: Machine learning

explanations.A: Incorrect. Data automation refers to automating data movement and processing tasks, not generating predictive suggestions that improve over time.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Trends analysis describes historical patterns but does not learn and continuously improve predictions from new data the way the requirement demands.
explanations.C: Correct. Machine learning uses all available data to make predictions and continually improves its suggestions as it is trained on more data, exactly matching the requirement for predictive, self-improving recommendations.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Multiple regression is a single statistical technique; it is one possible tool but does not by itself describe a system that continually learns and improves over time as machine learning does.

question: After rolling out a new update, an organization found a minor bug in its online video game. How should the organization approach this bug while following SRE principles?

options.A: Accept and learn from the bug because failure is normal
options.B: Accept and ignore the bug because it is only minor
options.C: Hold a postmortem to reprimand the employee responsible for the bug
options.D: Document bug correction to eliminate all future bugs

explanations.A: Correct. Site Reliability Engineering treats failure as an expected part of operating systems and emphasizes blameless learning, so the organization should accept the bug and learn from it to improve reliability.
explanations.B: Incorrect. SRE does not advocate ignoring problems; even minor bugs should be understood and learned from, not dismissed.
explanations.C: Incorrect. SRE promotes blameless postmortems focused on systemic causes, not reprimanding individuals, which would discourage transparency.
explanations.D: Incorrect. SRE accepts that eliminating all future bugs is impossible; the goal is managing reliability within acceptable error budgets, not achieving perfection.

question: Why do organizations often struggle to scale their on-premises application infrastructure?

options.A: Scaling compute instances could breach compliance and/or regulation
options.B: Increasing compute capacity is time-consuming and costly
options.C: Their serverless compute functions struggle to meet the demand
options.D: Their multi-cloud architecture is complex and expensive

explanations.A: Incorrect. Scaling compute does not inherently breach compliance; the real on-premises challenge is the effort and expense of adding capacity, not regulation.
explanations.B: Correct. Scaling on-premises requires procuring, installing, and configuring new physical hardware, which is slow and capital-intensive, making it hard to respond quickly to changing demand.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Serverless functions are a cloud capability, not part of traditional on-premises infrastructure, so they are not the reason on-premises scaling is hard.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Multi-cloud architecture is unrelated to the question of scaling an on-premises data center's hardware.

question: An organization wants to use BigQuery data analytics to understand their website performance, but wants to move only some data into the cloud. Which environment should the organization use?

options.A: Private cloud
options.B: On-premises
options.C: Multi-cloud

explanations.A: Incorrect. A private cloud keeps everything in a dedicated private environment and does not describe combining on-premises systems with a public service like BigQuery.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Staying fully on-premises would not let the organization use BigQuery, which is a Google Cloud service.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Multi-cloud refers to using more than one public cloud provider, not to keeping some data on-premises while using one cloud service.
explanations.D: Correct. A hybrid cloud combines on-premises infrastructure with public cloud, letting the organization keep most data locally while moving only the needed data into BigQuery for analytics.

question: What is logging within the context of cloud technology?

options.A: Writing application and operating system events as text
options.B: Monitoring network and resource limitations
options.C: Tracking source code across an organization

explanations.A: Correct. Logging is the recording of discrete application and operating system events as timestamped text entries, which can later be searched and analyzed for troubleshooting and auditing.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Watching network and resource limits is monitoring, which tracks metrics and health, not the recording of event records that defines logging.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Tracking source code is the role of version control systems, not logging.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Recording infrastructure and hardware spending is cost or billing management, not logging of system events.
